Rajesh —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, I'm sending the first-pass crosswalk that separates the control plane (management/telemetry/auth) from the data plane (inference traffic/KV cache). The attached PDF (control-data-crosswalk-v1.pdf) contains a one-page matrix plus a short diagram set.

Can you review and confirm the following items for Crestview:
- Whether you need the control plane to terminate TLS (mTLS) inside your VPC vs. at an isolated management proxy
- IP ranges and NAT behavior for egress (do you require static egress IPs?)
- Any specific telemetry/retention constraints (S3 vs. on-prem collector)

We're prepping an annotated diagram pack (Jonas is putting final touches) and we can schedule a 60-minute deep-dive next week for the network/infra teams. Proposed slots: Tue/Thu 11:00–13:00 PT.

Attachments: control-data-crosswalk-v1.pdf

Sean — thanks, got the PDF and the matrix. Couple quick clarifying questions before we go into the deep dive:

1) TLS/mTLS termination: our security team prefers that management connections terminate within our VPC (we hold the certs), but we can accept an authenticated reverse-proxy if Redwood can prove mutual-auth and audit logs. Can you outline the mutual auth handshake you expect?
2) Egress IPs: we need a proposal for static egress or a stable NAT solution. Is that something Redwood expects customers to provide, or can it be part of the deployment?
3) KV cache traffic: we need to understand whether cache replication flows cross our tenancy boundary. We can't allow cross-tenant KV replication.

I've attached our requirements workbook (crestview-vpc-requirements.xlsx) — it has the security checklist and our preferred CIDR blocks.

Available for the deep-dive Tue 11:30 PT.

Thanks,
Rajesh

Subject: Re: Split-plane crosswalk + annotated diagram pack for private VPC handoff

Rajesh —

Thanks for the workbook. I've attached an annotated diagram set that addresses the three bullets you raised. High-level summary below (see attachments: splitplane-annotated-diagram-v2.png, controlplane-dataflow-catalog.pdf):

- TLS/mTLS: control-plane management connections are designed to terminate inside the customer VPC. We support two modes:
  * Customer-managed certs (recommended): your PKI issues certs; control-plane agents use mTLS directly to the management endpoint inside the VPC.
  * Proxy-managed certs: if you prefer, a management-proxy (in your VPC) terminates mTLS and forwards a short-lived mutual-auth token to Redwood control-plane endpoints over an encrypted link. We log the proxy handshake for audit.

- Egress / static IPs: there are two supported options:
  1) Customer-provided NAT Gateway with static elastic IP (preferred for compliance).
  2) Customer-managed transit (e.g., static egress via colo) with a pinned BGP route to a Redwood ingress; Redwood can document expected source ASN and route preferences for peering.
  Note: Redwood does not provide shared static egress IPs for customer workloads in private deploys — we recommend option (1) for a guaranteed static egress address.

- KV cache replication: cache nodes are strictly within your data plane. By default there is no cross-tenant replication. If you opt into a shared caching tier (rare), that would be explicit and contractual. Default behavior: KV traffic stays inside your VPC fabric and uses VPC-internal routing (no public hops).

Operational notes / attachments:
- splitplane-annotated-diagram-v2.png: shows control-plane agents, management-proxy pattern, and telemetry collectors with sample port lists (443/tcp for mgmt; 9000/tcp for telemetry collector).
- controlplane-dataflow-catalog.pdf: table mapping logical flows to firewall rules and QoS classes.

Open items for the deep dive:
- Kimberly, can you confirm retention window and whether the collector can push to their S3/MinIO?
- Rajesh, if you confirm static NAT is available we'll mark egress as approved in the acceptance matrix.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber | Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Attachments: splitplane-annotated-diagram-v2.png; controlplane-dataflow-catalog.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the deep dive.

—Sean
